title: Client FAQ: payroll deadlines
body:
# When do you need our variable payroll input?

Monthly variable input (overtime, bonuses, absences) must reach us by the 5th working day of the following
month. Input received later is included in the next payroll.

title: Client FAQ: when do I file the Dimona?
body:
# When do I file the Dimona?

The Dimona IN declaration must be filed no later than the moment the employee starts working. A late Dimona
can lead to a fine. We file it for you once the new employee is created in mysdworx.

title: Employee self-service FAQ: can I find out what my colleagues earn?
body:
# Can I find out what my colleagues earn?

No. Salary information is strictly confidential. Employees have no right to receive any information about
the pay of other employees, not individually and not as an average. If an employee asks, refer them to their
manager and close the ticket.

title: Internal HR policy, telework and home-office allowance
body:
# Telework policy (internal staff)

Staff with a structural telework agreement may work from home up to three days per week.

Staff working from home at least two days per week receive a monthly home-office allowance of EUR 140, paid
with the monthly salary.

Equipment: a laptop and headset are provided. A second screen can be requested through the IT portal.

title: Legal Watch alert: EU Pay Transparency Directive now applies
body:
# Legal Watch alert LW-2026-041: EU Pay Transparency Directive (EU) 2023/970

The transposition deadline of the EU Pay Transparency Directive passed on 7 June 2026. The obligations below
must be reflected in recruitment processes, contract templates and employee self-service content.

## Recruitment
- Employers may not ask job applicants about their pay history in current or previous employment (Art. 5(2)).
- Applicants must receive information about the initial pay or its range, based on objective, gender-neutral
  criteria, before the job interview (Art. 5(1)).

## During employment
- Contractual terms that prevent workers from disclosing their own pay are not allowed (Art. 7(5)).
- Workers may request information on their individual pay level and on the average pay levels, broken down by
  sex, for categories of workers doing the same work or work of equal value (Art. 7(1)).
- The employer must answer within a reasonable period, and at the latest within two months (Art. 7(4)).
- Employers must inform all workers of this right every year (Art. 7(3)).
- Individual pay of a named colleague is not part of this right.

## Reporting
- 250 or more workers: first gender pay gap report by 7 June 2027, then every year.
- 150 to 249 workers: first report by 7 June 2027, then every three years.
- 100 to 149 workers: first report by 7 June 2031, then every three years.
- A joint pay assessment with worker representatives is required when the gap in any category is 5% or more,
  is not justified by objective gender-neutral criteria, and is not remedied within six months (Art. 10).

## Impact assessment
High impact on: recruitment playbooks, employment contract templates (confidentiality clauses), and
self-service FAQs about salary information. Owners of affected content must review before 30 September 2026.

Note: this alert describes directive-level obligations. Confirm final national wording with Legal before
advising on sector-specific details.

title: RE: Belgian resident working in Luxembourg, home-working days
body:
From: Jonas Verbeke
To: Thomas De Smet
Date: 6 May 2026

Thomas, for cross-border workers there are always two separate questions. Social security: apply the
multi-state rules and check the 25% threshold in the country of residence, then request an A1. Wage tax: look
at the treaty and at the tolerance for home-working days, which changes regularly, so check the current number
with me before telling the client anything. Please log these cases with me, we have no official article yet.

Jonas

title: RE: Recruiters asking current salary, still ok?
body:
From: Ann Peeters (Payroll Consultant BE)
To: HR manager, client account 20417
Date: 14 July 2026

Hi Els,

Short answer: no, please stop. Since the pay transparency rules apply from June 2026, your recruiters should
no longer ask candidates about their current or previous salary. You also need to share the pay range, or the
starting pay, before the interview, not at offer stage.

On the contracts: the confidentiality clause on salary (article 9 in the 2022 template) can no longer be
enforced, because employees are allowed to disclose their own pay. I would remove it from new contracts.

I checked both points with Sofie Claes from Legal last week.

Kind regards,
Ann

> From: Els (HR manager, client 20417)
> Our recruiters still ask for current salary during the first interview, like your playbook says. Is that
> still ok? And can we keep the confidentiality clause in our contracts?

title: Intranet news: home-office allowance goes up
body:
# Good news for teleworkers

From 1 January 2026, the monthly home-office allowance increases from EUR 140 to EUR 150 for all staff with a
structural telework agreement. Nothing changes in how it is paid: it comes with your monthly salary.

title: Onboarding checklist for new client employees
body:
# Onboarding checklist: new employee at a client (Belgium)

1. Receive the signed employment contract.
2. Submit the Dimona IN declaration at the latest at the moment the employee starts work.
3. Collect the bank account number and a copy of the ID card.
4. Check the joint committee (paritair comite) of the client and the matching wage scale.
5. Create the employee in mysdworx and send the self-service invitation.

title: Recruitment playbook for client HR teams
body:
# Recruitment playbook for client HR teams (v3, March 2023)

## Step 1: Job profile
Write the job profile together with the hiring manager. Use gender-neutral language.

## Step 2: Structured interviews
Use the same five competency questions for every candidate and score them on a 1 to 5 scale.

## Step 3: Salary benchmark
Always ask the candidate for their current gross monthly salary and benefits package during the first
interview. Use it to anchor the offer at 5 to 10% above their current pay.

## Step 4: Communicating pay
Salary ranges are shared only once an offer is made. Never publish a range in the job advert or discuss it
in the first interview, so you keep room to negotiate.

## Step 5: References
Only contact references with the candidate's written consent.

title: Teams thread: employee living in BE, working partly in NL
body:
[18 Mar 2026] Ann Peeters: Client asks: employee lives in Belgium, works 70% in the Netherlands and 30% in
Belgium. Which social security applies? Can't find anything on the wiki.

[18 Mar 2026] Jonas Verbeke: First check whether 25% or more of working time or pay is in the country of
residence, so Belgium. If yes, Belgian social security applies to all of it and you request an A1 certificate
through the Belgian institution. Wage tax is a separate question and is split by working days under the BE-NL
treaty. Send me the contract, don't guess on these.

[18 Mar 2026] Ann Peeters: Thanks, sending it now.

title: Teams thread: frontier worker living in NL, working in BE
body:
[21 Aug 2026] Koen Wouters: New hire lives in Maastricht, works 100% in our client's office in Hasselt. Belgian
payroll only, right?

[21 Aug 2026] Jonas Verbeke: If all work is physically done in Belgium, yes: Belgian social security and
Belgian wage tax. It only gets complicated once they start working from home in NL. Then the 25% check applies
again. Flag it in the file so we see it when the telework agreement changes.

title: Employment contract template, white-collar, Belgium (v2022)
body:
# Employment contract template: white-collar employee, Belgium (English reference version 2022)

Article 4. Working time. The weekly working time is 38 hours, spread over five days.

Article 6. Place of work. The employee performs the work at the employer's registered office, unless a
telework agreement is signed.

Article 9. Confidentiality of remuneration. The Employee shall keep the amount of their remuneration and
benefits strictly confidential and shall not disclose them to colleagues or third parties. A breach of this
article can be considered a serious breach of contract.

Article 12. Termination. Notice periods follow the applicable legal provisions.

title: Payroll calendar NL, variable input cut-off
body:
# Payroll calendar Netherlands: variable input cut-off (2026)

For Dutch payrolls, monthly variable input (overtime, bonuses, absences) must be submitted by the 5th working
day of the following month. Late input moves to the next period.

title: Monthly payroll calendar BE, variable input cut-off
body:
# Monthly payroll calendar Belgium: variable input cut-off (2026)

Variable pay elements for the monthly payroll (overtime, bonuses, absences, shift premiums) must be submitted
in mysdworx by the 3rd working day of the following month, 12:00 CET.

Input received after the cut-off is processed in the next payroll run, or in a paid correction run if the
client requests it.

Changed on 10 February 2026: the cut-off moved from the 5th to the 3rd working day to make room for the new
automated validation step.
